title: Crown and Oath Again
premise: When the border wards over the Thornfell mountains collapse on the night the stars vanish, gate-keeper Rafael Eriksen discovers the wards were fed by a stolen soul — the soul of their dead brother, sold decades ago to the court that rules beneath the mountain. To restore the wards and bring back the stars, Rafael must cross into the Undercourt with a disgraced oathbreaker knight, a smuggler who owes them a blood debt, and a child who can hear the mountain dreaming. But the Undercourt's law is older and crueler than any kingdom's: debts may be reclaimed, but only by trading a soul of equal weight. Rafael ends the story by offering their own name in place of their brother's, breaking the court's ledger and forcing the mountain to release every soul it holds — an act of justice no crown ever sanctioned, paid for with the gate Rafael swore to keep.
about_author: Sebastian Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border treaties and smugglers' confessions before turning to fantasy. They write about people who keep promises the law forgot, and live somewhere within sight of mountains they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Gate That Should Stay Shut
chapters.summary: Rafael Eriksen's POV. A quiet night of gate-keeping in Thornfell establishes Rafael's routines, their grief for a brother dead twenty years, and their knowledge of every smuggler's path through the mountains. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as duty, the calm before catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The wards fail at midnight and every star vanishes at once; smugglers, soldiers, and strangers stumble through the dark gate together. Rafael recognizes the ward-signature in the collapse as their dead brother's soul-mark. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into terrible recognition.

chapters.title: An Oathbreaker at the Door
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with interludes from Ser Maren Kael. Maren, a knight stripped of her oath for telling a truth the crown buried, arrives seeking the gate-keeper's help. Rafael refuses — until she reveals the crown knew the wards ran on stolen souls. Emotional beat: distrust between two people betrayed by the same crown.

chapters.title: What the Smuggler Owes
chapters.summary: Dax Ferrow's POV. Smuggler Dax Ferrow owes Rafael a blood debt from a winter crossing gone wrong, and hates that the ward-fall has stranded his crew in the dark. He agrees to guide them through the mountain's underside — for a price. Emotional beat: resentment curdling into reluctant loyalty.

chapters.title: The Child Who Hears the Mountain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In a refugee camp beneath the dead stars, the party finds Wren, an orphan who hums songs no one taught her — songs the mountain sings in its sleep. Wren claims the mountain is counting souls and coming up short. Emotional beat: found family's first fragile spark.

chapters.title: Roads That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Dax's POV. The party descends through smuggler tunnels that have rearranged themselves since the stars went out, as if the mountain is hiding something. Rafael's map-knowledge fails for the first time in their life. Emotional beat: the humbling of expertise, dependence on strangers.

chapters.title: The First Toll
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A bridge of roots demands a memory as toll. Maren pays with the truth that destroyed her knighthood, and Rafael learns the crown sold souls to the Undercourt to win a war no history records. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The party reaches the Undercourt: a cathedral of bone and lamplight where the soulless serve the gentry of the deep. They see their brother's soul — or its echo — wearing a servant's collar. Emotional beat: hope and horror arriving hand in hand.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Deep
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The court's Ledger-Keeper confirms the debt: one soul, sold, still owed, and the stars will stay dark until it is returned. But the ledger cannot be edited — only balanced. Emotional beat: the cold arithmetic of justice without mercy.

chapters.title: Wren's Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, rendered in her simple, eerie voice. Wren dreams the mountain's dream: it does not want the soul back, it wants a keeper. The gate was never Rafael's to hold — it was the mountain's leash. Emotional beat: a child carrying an adult's dread.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Choice
chapters.summary: Dax's POV. Dax's crew, hunted by the court's bailiffs, is offered freedom if they betray the party's route. Dax burns his own maps instead, choosing Rafael over his livelihood. Emotional beat: a debt repaid becomes a bond freely given.

chapters.title: What Maren Buried
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren confesses fully: the truth she spoke was that the crown's victory war was won with purchased souls — and her king ordered her silenced. Rafael realizes their brother was sold to end a war that never needed fighting. Emotional beat: rage seeking a target, finding a cause.

chapters.title: The Bailiff's Hunt
chapters.summary: Dax's POV. The court's bailiffs corner the party in the lamplight markets; Wren's humming unravels the bailiffs' bindings and the group escapes into the deep dark. Maren is wounded. Emotional beat: fear transformed into ferocity — no one gets left behind.

chapters.title: The Soul That Remembers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael reaches their brother's soul-echo and speaks to it; it remembers nothing but the gate, and the keeping. The echo begs not to be freed but to be finished. Emotional beat: love confronting the fact that rescue and release are not the same.

chapters.title: A Debt of Equal Weight
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The Ledger-Keeper offers the terms: the brother's soul returns to the wards if a soul of equal weight takes its place in the ledger. Maren volunteers; Rafael refuses to let her. Dax quietly does the same. Emotional beat: found family competing to sacrifice for each other.

chapters.title: The Mountain's True Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren leads them to the mountain's dreaming heart and speaks its true name aloud, which no one has dared in a thousand years. The mountain wakes, and the court's authority over souls begins to crack. Emotional beat: the smallest member of the family doing the impossible.

chapters.title: Crown and Oath Again
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The court's regent offers Rafael a crown of the deep: become the mountain's keeper, and all debts dissolve. Rafael sees the trap — a keeper is just a soul the mountain owns — and instead re-swears their gate-oath in the mountain's own hearing. Emotional beat: refusing power in favor of promise.

chapters.title: The Ledger Breaks
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Rafael writes their own name into the ledger in place of their brother's — not as payment, but as a claim: a keeper's name outranks a debtor's under the old law. The ledger splits down its spine, and every caged soul in the court goes free at once. Emotional beat: triumph bought at the brink of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Stars Return
chapters.summary: Dax's POV. The freed souls stream back into the wards and the stars reignite over Thornfell; the brother's soul, released rather than bound, chooses to pass on, thanking Rafael with a touch like morning frost. Emotional beat: grief finally allowed to end.

chapters.title: What Rafael Paid
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Rafael's name is fading from the ledger and from memory; Wren refuses to forget, singing Rafael's name into the mountain's dream so it can never be erased. Emotional beat: love outlasting law, memory as resistance.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Gate
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael stands at their gate, name half-gone but oath intact, and finds the mountain has answered Wren's song: it names Rafael its keeper freely, restoring the name with interest. Maren, Dax, and Wren choose to stay. Emotional beat: the found family, complete, choosing each other in daylight.

chapters.title: Oath Kept, Gate Open
chapters.summary: Ensemble epilogue, Rafael's POV closing. The gate reopens — not shut, as the old law demanded, but watched, honest, and fair, with the mountain's own law and the crown's old wards replaced by something better. Rafael lights the gate-lamp for the first traveler. Emotional beat: peace earned, justice kept outside the law and inside the heart.
